fallback.text: A 1 kg mass on a spring (k = 4 N/m) is pulled 1 m aside and let go. With light damping (c = 0.2 N·s/m) it swings for a long time and about 60 % of its energy is still there after 2.5 s; with c = 1.6 N·s/m the swings die out quickly and only about 2 % is left. The damping force −c·v takes the energy away; the spring alone only trades it between motion and stretch.
